title: The host galaxy of the short GRB 050709
question: Characterize the physical properties (star formation rate, metallicity, gas kinematics, excitation mechanisms, merger history) of the host galaxy of short GRB 050709 and constrain late-time radio emission.

data.sensitivity: 5 sigma rms upper limit of 55 uJy beam^-1

what.value: Host galaxy stellar mass log M_star/M_sun = 8.8

evidence.quote: According to these authors, the SED reveals a dominating stellar population with an age of about 2 Gyr and a stellar mass of log M ⋆ / M ⊙ = 8.8.
its stellar mass (log M⋆/M⊙= 8.8; Leibler & Berger 2010)

what.value: Host galaxy B-band absolute magnitude M_B = -16.9 ± 0.1

evidence.quote: According to Hjorth et al. (2005), the host of GRB 050709 is a blue dwarf galaxy with an absolute magnitude M B = −16.9 ± 0.1.

what.value: MAGMA sample of local star-forming galaxies for mass-metallicity and star-formation main sequence comparisons

evidence.quote: The galaxies illustrated in the mass–metallicity relation (MZR) are taken from the MAGMA (Metallicity and Gas for Mass Assembly) sample of local star-forming galaxies (e.g., Ginolfi et al. 2020; Hunt et al. 2020).

external_data.citation: Ginolfi et al. 2020; Hunt et al. 2020

what.value: Galactic foreground reddening E(B - V) = 0.01 mag

evidence.quote: The data were corrected for Galactic foreground reddening ( E ( B − V ) = 0.01 mag; Schlafly & Finkbeiner 2011), assuming an average Milky Way extinction law (Pei 1992) and R V = 3.08.

recipe.goal: Reduce and image ALMA 1.3 mm continuum data and derive SFR upper limit
recipe.method: Combine two ALMA Band 6 execution blocks in CASA tclean, measure 5 sigma rms upper limit at phase center, and convert to SFR upper limit using redshifted and renormalized Chary & Elbaz (2001) IR SED templates and the Kennicutt (1998) relation.
assumptions: z = 0.1606, H_0 = 68 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_M = 0.31, Omega_Lambda = 0.69

recipe.goal: Reduce Spitzer 24 um data and derive mid-IR SFR upper limit
recipe.method: Reduce MIPS 24 um data with MOPEX, measure sky noise in ten empty regions to derive 3 sigma flux upper limit following Dale et al. (2012), and convert to SFR using Tzanavaris et al. (2010) and Murphy et al. (2011) relations.
key_parameters: 10 empty sky regions, N_pix = N_sky slightly larger than MIPS PSF
assumptions: Spectral slope beta between 3 and 4 in L_nu ~ nu^-beta

recipe.goal: Reduce ATCA radio continuum data and measure fluxes/upper limits
recipe.method: Reduce ATCA 5.5 and 9.0 GHz visibilities in MIRIAD, image with robust weighting (0.0 to 2.0) and tapering, check astrometry against cataloged quasars, and derive upper limits on point-source afterglow/kilonova emission and extended emission flux.
key_parameters: Briggs robust = 0.0 to 2.0; uv taper FWHM = 5 arcsec
assumptions: Isotropic emission, spectral slope beta = -1/3 or 0.7 for radio AG and beta = 0.7 for kilonova flare

recipe.goal: Reduce VLT/MUSE IFU data and separate stellar and gas-phase emission
recipe.method: Reduce MUSE exposures with the ESO MUSE pipeline, remove telluric absorption with molecfit, align astrometry to HST/F814W with SAOimage DS9 using point source Q, correct for Galactic foreground extinction, and fit and subtract stellar continuum using Starlight with Bruzual & Charlot (2003) SSP models.
key_parameters: S/N >= 4 for bright lines (Halpha, [O III] 5007) and S/N >= 2 for faint lines (Hbeta, [N II] 6584, [S II] 6718)
assumptions: Galactic foreground E(B-V) = 0.01 mag, Milky Way extinction law (Pei 1992), R_V = 3.08

recipe.goal: Map host galaxy reddening, SFR, EW(Halpha), metallicity, kinematics, and BPT diagnostics
recipe.method: From spaxel emission line fluxes in the MUSE gas cube, compute E(B-V)_host via Balmer decrement, extinction-corrected SFR(Halpha) via Murphy et al. (2011), EW(Halpha), O3N2 oxygen abundance via Pettini & Pagel (2004), Halpha radial velocity and intrinsic velocity dispersion, and [N II] and [S II] BPT diagrams.
key_parameters: 2 arcsec radius aperture for global SFR; continuum flux density >= 2e-20 erg s^-1 cm^-2 A^-1 for EW(Halpha); sigma_instr = 42 km s^-1, sigma_T,gas = 9.1 km s^-1
assumptions: Case B recombination at T = 10^4 K, n_e ~ 10^2 - 10^4 cm^-3, intrinsic Halpha/Hbeta = 2.85, R_V = 3.08
Solar oxygen abundance 12 + log(O/H) = 8.69 (Asplund et al. 2009)
